title: Youtiao Twin Dough Sticks with Warm Soy Milk
summary: Crisp, hollow Chinese twin dough sticks served with a bowl of warm soy milk for dipping.
equipment: cling film or a lidded container
wok or wide heavy pan, at least 28 cm
wire rack over a tray lined with kitchen paper

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
neutral oil, plus extra for the surface
neutral frying oil (sunflower, rapeseed or vegetable)

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Whisk the flour, baking powder, bicarbonate and salt in the bowl. Beat the egg with the cold water and oil, pour it in and stir to a rough dough.

steps.title: Knead
steps.text: Knead for 3 min, cover and leave for 15 min, then knead for 2 min more until the dough is smooth and soft.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Shape it into a flat log of about 20 cm, rub it with a little oil, wrap it well and chill for 12-24 h. Take it out of the fridge 1 h before frying.

steps.title: Cut and pair
steps.text: Roll the dough on a lightly oiled surface into a strip 10 cm wide and 6 mm thick. Cut it into 16 strips 2.5 cm wide, lay them on top of each other in pairs and press a chopstick down firmly along the centre of each pair.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Fill the wok with oil to about 5 cm, no more than half full, and heat it to 200 °C.

steps.title: Fry
steps.text: Hold a pair by both ends, gently stretch it to about 25 cm and lower it into the oil. Keep turning it for 1.5-2 min at 190-200 °C, until it puffs to twice its size and turns deep golden and crisp. Drain on the rack and fry the rest one or two at a time.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Warm the soy milk with the sugar until steaming. Serve it in bowls with the hot sticks for dipping.

tips: The most common mistake is skipping the long rest; without it the dough will not stretch or puff.
Turn the sticks constantly in the first seconds so they puff evenly.
Very hot oil is essential; below 190 °C they stay dense and greasy.
Use oil, not flour, on the surface so the pairs stay stuck together.

Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
storage: Best eaten within an hour. Re-crisp leftovers in a 200 °C oven for 4-5 min. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
